**Question 1.** Can location and time predict whether a registered EV is fully battery-electric (BEV)
rather than a plug-in hybrid (PHEV)?

Uses the cleaned data from Part 1 (render `01_data_preparation_eda.Rmd` first). The Python version is
`python/02_q1_classification.ipynb`.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
# ---- Setup ----
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rpart)
library(randomForest)
library(pROC)

theme_set(theme_minimal())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5)

df <- read.csv("../data/processed/ev_clean_r.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
               colClasses = c(zip = "character", leg_district = "character"))
df$log_city_evs <- log10(df$city_evs)
cat(sprintf("Rows: %d; BEV share: %.2f%%\n", nrow(df), 100 * mean(df$bev)))
```

# 1. Approach

As in Python: features are model year, log10 EVs in the city, region, county group, primary utility and
legislative district (no make, model, range or incentive eligibility). Numeric features are
standardized; categorical ones are factors. The logistic regression and tree use class weights; the
random forest draws balanced samples. The random forest is trained on an 80,000-vehicle subsample of
the training set and cross-validation uses a 50,000-vehicle subsample. Metrics: ROC-AUC, balanced
accuracy, BEV recall/precision/F1 and PHEV recall.

```{r split}
num_cols <- c("model_year", "log_city_evs")
cat_cols <- c("region", "county_grp", "utility", "leg_district")
data <- df[, c(num_cols, cat_cols)]
data[cat_cols] <- lapply(data[cat_cols], factor)
data$type <- factor(ifelse(df$bev == 1, "BEV", "PHEV"), levels = c("PHEV", "BEV"))

set.seed(42)
idx <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$type), function(i) sample(i, round(0.8 * length(i)))))
train <- data[idx, ]
test <- data[-idx, ]
mu <- sapply(train[num_cols], mean); sdv <- sapply(train[num_cols], sd)
train[num_cols] <- sweep(sweep(train[num_cols], 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")
test[num_cols] <- sweep(sweep(test[num_cols], 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")
cat("Training:", nrow(train), " Test:", nrow(test), "\n")

# Sanity check: make alone (without model) already largely determines the type
mm <- data.frame(make = factor(df$Make), type = data$type)
mm_tr <- mm[idx, ]; mm_te <- mm[-idx, ]
mm_te <- mm_te[mm_te$make %in% unique(mm_tr$make), ]
fit_mm <- glm(type ~ make, data = mm_tr, family = binomial)
cat(sprintf("Sanity check, make only: test AUC = %.4f\n",
            as.numeric(auc(mm_te$type, predict(fit_mm, mm_te, type = "response"), quiet = TRUE))))
```

# 2. Training and evaluation

```{r models}
wts <- function(y) ifelse(y == "BEV", length(y) / (2 * sum(y == "BEV")), length(y) / (2 * sum(y == "PHEV")))
fit_predict <- function(m, tr, te) {
  if (m == "Logistic regression") {
    f <- glm(type ~ ., data = tr, family = quasibinomial, weights = wts(tr$type))
    p <- predict(f, te, type = "response")
  } else if (m == "Decision tree") {
    f <- rpart(type ~ ., data = tr, weights = wts(tr$type), method = "class",
               control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 6, minbucket = 200, cp = 0))
    p <- predict(f, te, type = "prob")[, "BEV"]
  } else {
    n_min <- min(table(tr$type))
    f <- randomForest(type ~ ., data = tr, ntree = 200, nodesize = 50, strata = tr$type,
                      sampsize = c(n_min, n_min))
    p <- predict(f, te, type = "prob")[, "BEV"]
  }
  list(fit = f, p = p)
}
models <- c("Logistic regression", "Decision tree", "Random forest")
auc_of <- function(y, p) as.numeric(auc(y, p, levels = c("PHEV", "BEV"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE))

set.seed(1)
cv_set <- train[sample(nrow(train), 50000), ]
folds <- integer(nrow(cv_set))
for (cl in levels(cv_set$type)) { i <- which(cv_set$type == cl); folds[i] <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out = length(i))) }
cv_auc <- sapply(models, function(m) sapply(1:5, function(k) {
  r <- fit_predict(m, cv_set[folds != k, ], cv_set[folds == k, ]); auc_of(cv_set$type[folds == k], r$p)
}))

set.seed(42)
rf_rows <- sample(nrow(train), 80000)
fits <- lapply(setNames(models, models), function(m)
  fit_predict(m, if (m == "Random forest") train[rf_rows, ] else train, test))

results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
  p <- fits[[m]]$p; pred <- ifelse(p >= 0.5, "BEV", "PHEV"); y <- test$type
  rec_b <- mean(pred[y == "BEV"] == "BEV"); rec_p <- mean(pred[y == "PHEV"] == "PHEV")
  prec_b <- mean(y[pred == "BEV"] == "BEV")
  data.frame(model = m, cv_auc = sprintf("%.3f +/- %.3f", mean(cv_auc[, m]), sd(cv_auc[, m])),
             test_auc = round(auc_of(y, p), 3), balanced_accuracy = round((rec_b + rec_p) / 2, 3),
             bev_recall = round(rec_b, 3), bev_precision = round(prec_b, 3),
             bev_f1 = round(2 * rec_b * prec_b / (rec_b + prec_b), 3), phev_recall = round(rec_p, 3))
}))
results
```

```{r roc, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 5.5}
roc_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(models, function(m) {
  r <- roc(test$type, fits[[m]]$p, levels = c("PHEV", "BEV"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
  data.frame(model = sprintf("%s (AUC = %.3f)", m, as.numeric(r$auc)), fpr = 1 - r$specificities,
             tpr = r$sensitivities)
}))
ggplot(roc_df, aes(fpr, tpr, colour = model)) + geom_line() + geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "ROC Curves on the Test Set (BEV = positive)", x = "False positive rate",
       y = "True positive rate (BEV recall)", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

**Interpretation.** Test ROC-AUC ranges from `r min(results$test_auc)` to `r max(results$test_auc)`; the
tree-based models beat logistic regression because the BEV share changes non-linearly with model year.

# 3. Which factors matter?

```{r importance}
rf <- fits[["Random forest"]]$fit
set.seed(42)
te <- test[sample(nrow(test), 20000), ]
base <- auc_of(te$type, predict(rf, te, type = "prob")[, "BEV"])
feats <- c(num_cols, cat_cols)
drops <- sapply(feats, function(f) mean(replicate(3, {
  s <- te; s[[f]] <- sample(s[[f]]); base - auc_of(te$type, predict(rf, s, type = "prob")[, "BEV"])
})))
imp <- data.frame(feature = feats, mean_auc_drop = round(drops, 4)) %>% arrange(desc(mean_auc_drop))
ggplot(imp, aes(reorder(feature, mean_auc_drop), mean_auc_drop)) + geom_col(fill = "seagreen") + coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Random Forest: Permutation Importance", x = "Feature",
       y = "Drop in test ROC-AUC when the feature is shuffled")
imp

or <- exp(coef(fits[["Logistic regression"]]$fit))
round(or[c("model_year", "log_city_evs", grep("^region|^utility", names(or), value = TRUE))], 3)
```

```{r save}
write.csv(results, "../report/figures/q1_results_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(imp, "../report/figures/q1_permutation_importance_r.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# 4. Discussion

The R results agree with Python. Model year is again by far the most important feature (AUC drop
`r imp$mean_auc_drop[imp$feature == "model_year"]`, against at most
`r max(imp$mean_auc_drop[imp$feature != "model_year"])` for any location feature), and each standard
deviation of model year multiplies the odds of a BEV by `r round(or["model_year"], 2)`. Vehicles in the
Seattle metro have `r round(or["regionSeattle metro"], 2)` times the odds of eastern Washington vehicles,
much less than in Python (1.29): region and county overlap (each county belongs to one region), and R's
unpenalized logistic regression attributes the effect to the county terms, whereas scikit-learn's default
L2 penalty spreads it across both. The overall region effect is the same in the raw data (82.5% BEV in
the Seattle metro against 75.5% in eastern Washington).
Location and time predict vehicle type only modestly (AUC about 0.62–0.65); brand and model, excluded on
purpose, are what really determine it. Small differences from Python come from the different random
split and the random forest's balanced sampling instead of class weights.
